messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Analysis for activPAL data
parts:
Hi John,

This functionality has never been well tested as I only had one example file at the time and never used it in projects, so it would be good to investigate a bit more.

Could you store the output of your read.myacc.csv call to an object as in:

data = read.myacc.csv(rmc.file ...

Next, explore whether there is anything strange about these timestamps. For example with:

mean(round(data$data$timestamp))

rounds all timestamps and takes the average, this may already reproduce the error you got, which would be good to know.

table(is.na(test$data$timestamp))

should be FALSE only, if you see TRUE then that would mean there are missing values.

table(diff(data$data$timestamp))

shows the distribution in timesteps between successive timestamps. These should all be somewhere between 0 and 0.06 and not negative or large.

range(test$data$timestamp)

should show the timestamp range in your data, is it plausible?

Thanks, Vincent

Hi Vincent

I have done the testing as per your suggestion, and below is what I found:

data <- read.myacc.csv(rmc.file = "C:/Users/khchong/Documents/PAL/Data/3001.csv",
                       rmc.nrow = Inf,
                       rmc.skip = 0,

rmc.dec = ".",
                       rmc.firstrow.acc = 2,
                       rmc.col.acc = 3:5,
                       rmc.col.time=1,

rmc.unit.time = "ActivPAL",
                       rmc.desiredtz = "Australia/Sydney",
                       rmc.configtz = "Australia/Sydney",
                       rmc.sf = 20)

> mean(round(data$data$timestamp))
[1] "2019-02-22 23:01:00 AEDT"
> table(is.na(data$data$timestamp))

   FALSE 
12095975 
> table(diff(data$data$timestamp))

0.0499987602233887 0.0499992370605469 0.0499997138977051 0.0500001907348633 0.0500078201293945 0.0500082969665527 0.0500087738037109 
            268799             670207           10375658             333311              93184             193536             161279 
> range(data$data$timestamp)
[1] "2019-02-19 11:01:01 AEDT" "2019-02-26 11:00:59 AEDT"

So I didn't get any errors from the testing and was able to get the results that you mentioned for each line of code. However, something isn't right with the timestamp. The time for the first row of data was displayed as 11:01AM on 2019-02-19; however, it should be 12:01:01 AM instead. The device was initialised to collect data in the same time zone as per the script, i.e. "Australia/Sydney".

I have attached the csv data file here to help you with the investigations.
 3001.csv

Thank you.

Best regards,
John.
